title: incident-bot: suggest runbook fixes and autofix UI for SLO diagnostics
author: Priya Desai
description: Add a new autofix suggestions flow to incident-bot that surfaces runnable runbook edits when SLO diagnostics detect a likely missing or outdated remediation step. Motivation: on recent incidents we observed repetitive operator fixes that could be automated or at least suggested to the on-call via vetted runbook edits. This PR implements: 1) diagnostic-to-fix translator: a lightweight rule-based engine that converts common diagnostic patterns (e.g. KV cache warmup failures, model OOM, node scheduling saturations) into suggested runbook edits and an optional one-click patch. 2) UI hooks in the on-call message payloads that include a compact "Suggested fix" card with diff preview and an action button (Apply suggested runbook edit) gated behind a feature flag. 3) Telemetry for suggestion acceptance/ignore rates and post-apply outcomes for measuring correctness. 4) Rate-limiting and approval flow: suggestions are only auto-proposed if confidence >= 0.7 and we haven't suggested fixes for the same SLO within the last 24h; applying a suggested edit creates a changelist entry which requires a second approval from an owner before finalizing (configurable by org). 5) Tests and docs: unit tests for the rule engine, integration tests for message payloads, updated runbook docs and an ops playbook entry. Checklist: - [x] rule-based translator + tests - [x] message payloads and UI card - [x] feature flag + rollout config - [x] telemetry hooks + metrics - [x] rate limits + approval flow - [x] docs and release notes Notes: - This is behind the runtime feature flag "autofix_runbook_suggestions" (off by default). We intentionally keep the translator rule-based for now to limit scope; future follow-ups will evaluate ML-based suggestion ranking. - Security: applying suggestions requires Runbook write scope and is audited; we added an audit log event when a suggestion is applied or ignored. - Performance: suggestion generation runs asynchronously after diagnostics complete and is capped to 200ms per diagnostic to avoid impacting core pipelines. Follow-ups: ENG-9420 (ML ranking prototype), ENG-9481 (admin UI for approval policy), SRE-1201 (tune rule thresholds).
